mechanics.name: Deliverance
mechanics.currentEffect: After safely unhooking another Survivor, your next self-unhook attempt during the first Hook Stage succeeds. Afterward you suffer Broken for 160/140/120 seconds. Cannot activate if you are in the second Hook Stage or were hooked while the last Survivor remaining.
activation: Be hooked in the first Hook Stage and attempt to self-unhook.
Ends/deactivates when: Cannot activate after reaching the second Hook Stage or if hooked while last remaining.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.1.0): Changed post-self-unhook Broken duration to 160/140/120 seconds.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: A safe unhook lets you guarantee a self-unhook during your first Hook Stage, followed by Broken.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: Once per Trial; deactivates after successful self-unhook.
specialInteractions: A safe rescue means the rescued Survivor avoids a subsequent hit within the safe-unhook evaluation window.

editorial.summary: After a safe rescue, your first-stage self-unhook is guaranteed once, at the cost of a long Broken period.
useCases: Remove the need for a teammate to rotate across the map for your rescue.
Take an intentionally awkward chase or basement hook after the perk is armed.
Create powerful endgame Hook Trades because you can rescue someone and then free yourself.
counters: If the Killer finds and hooks you before you get a safe rescue, the perk does nothing.
A failed or unsafe rescue does not arm it.
The 120-second Tier III Broken duration makes the post-unhook reset much slower than before 10.1.
Second Hook Stage and last-Survivor situations disable its self-rescue value.
pros: Once armed, it gives you rescue independence with no teammate travel time.
Can make otherwise terrible hook locations strategically acceptable.
Has unusually high endgame leverage when trading for a teammate.
cons: The famous first-chase problem is real: early pressure can delete the perk before it activates.
Requires altruistic setup before it becomes useful.
The 10.1 Broken-duration nerf significantly delays healing after the self-unhook.
analysis: Deliverance creates value by deleting an entire rescue rotation. Once it is armed, the team knows that your first hook does not automatically require another Survivor to abandon a generator, cross the map, and expose themselves near the hook. That is a large tempo swing, especially late in a match when every few seconds on the final generators matter.

The price is reliability. If you are the first Survivor found and hooked, Deliverance is a dead perk slot. That makes positioning and early-match awareness part of the skill requirement even though the self-unhook itself is automatic. SWF can deliberately route the Deliverance user away from the first chase; Solo Q cannot guarantee that.

The 10.1.0 nerf matters. Tier III now leaves you Broken for 120 seconds instead of the much shorter historical duration, so Deliverance is no longer a clean self-rescue followed by an immediate reset. The perk is strongest when the time saved by not requiring a rescuer matters more than the delayed heal, which is often true in late game, split-pressure situations, and coordinated teams.

Shoulder the Burden can interact with Deliverance by changing Hook-State distribution, but both perks now carry major strategic costs. Even without that interaction, a guaranteed self-rescue remains unique enough to keep Deliverance a premium rescue perk.
editorial.verdict: Still a premium rescue perk after the 10.1 Broken nerf. The setup can fail, but once armed Deliverance changes the team’s rescue economy and can produce game-winning endgame trades.
